items.explanation: Past participle in passive getǣht wæs; him is the person to whom the route was indicated.
Prefixed movement verb; do not split into an unnoticed new finite gān spelling.
Inside the dependent question hwone ... biddan meahte; indicative/subjunctive surface coincides. The selected interpretation is possibility in the thought.
Exact source prefixed participle and retained w; distinct from selected unprefixed smierwan paradigm. Mid ęle marks the anointing material.
Passive/predicative participle with mid scīetan, a cloth.
Tō + dative bæðstęde identifies what the games/equipment relate to; preserve source note6.
The new productive cry sense; micelre stefne is a dative of manner/instrument.
Exact plural command with shortened -e before following gē, not singular by surface alone. The same form recurs later in the line.
Hine is the person undressed; ðǣm healfan sciccelse is the removed clothing, supplied case frame.
Accusative persons observed; no modern behold quotation formula implied.
On ðæt bæð gives the entry destination.
StrongIII preterite of āginnan, not āgan own/possess and not āgān depart.
Infinitive after began; wið + dative companions and mid + dative ball are supported locally.
Reflexive hine; on ðæs cyninges plegan continues on169.1. Plegan is an oblique noun governed by on; ðæs cyninges is its genitive possessor. It is not a finite verb.
Joined across printed line break iern-/ende; the supplied participle accompanies Apollonius. Do not count the two printed fragments as two words.
Exact source preterite has short æ as printed; preserve lexical spelling and do not silently import a guessed long form.
Exact accusative participle agreeing with ðone ðoðor, an evidenced exceptional -e form noted by Cook; do not regularize to a new target.
Tō + dative recipient; ongēan is the return direction.
Weak dative modifier of cyninge after ðǣm; the finite paradigm does not itself teach this participial cell.
Exact source singular h spelling; Wright262–263 explicitly gives slōg/slōh. Preserve the earlier selected slōg system and supply this contextual variant.
Accusative snelnesse, followed by a result/content sequence whose pronoun referents remain genuinely underdetermined in Cook note6.
Accusative hine is the praised person; the exact source spelling remains.
New productive selected preterite.
The prefixed verb with tō + dative goal is supplied; do not rename it as the unprefixed nēalǣcan form.
Direct object top is the actual OE object. Do not substitute the Latin shoulder/rubbing action.
Supply ðǣm cyninge wæs geðūht swilce ... wǣre, it seemed to the king as though ...; dative experiencer and irrealis comparison are explicit.
In swilce hē of ielde tō geoguðe gewęnd wǣre: as though he had been turned from age to youth. Do not mechanically label every wesan+participle a motion perfect.
Dative him is the served person; exact source -ode spelling, not a fabricated finite ending from the infinitive.
Prefixed motion verb with of + dative place left.
Reflexive dative him; ðæs weges is the route genitive, matched by the composition35.3. Pronoun references need discourse reasoning.
Past participle in āgān wæs, had departed. Distinguish unmacroned āgan began at168.17.
First-person quoted oath; ðurh + accusative oath standard; the narrated speaker now owns ic.
Reflexive mē and adverbial comparison with dyde; this bath verb is supplied, substitute dōn is newly productive.
Exact contracted negative witan lexeme/form is supplied; no full nytan system was taught earlier or is introduced here.
Reflexive hine and tō + dative person toward whom he turned; supply as a local phrase.
The preterite-present knowing verb (§126), not strongI gewītan depart; the dependent question has hwæt ... sīe.
Dative mē is the person served; hyphenation gehīer-/sumode is print line division only.
Mid + dative garment in the passive/predicative description.
Ongēan + tō destination; distinct from wēnan expected despite the similar modern gloss.
Æfter links to the relative antecedent; exact source spelling preserves -odest.
Ðēah concessive clause; hit is the thing withheld. Exact source ending is supplied rather than silently generalized to a weak-II table.
Gegierela is the singular subject, hine the person whose condition is revealed.
Exact source shortened command spelling; the following mixed direct/indirect quotation is explicitly supported by Cook note15, not presented as a regular report transformation.
